concept.name: Equilibrium level
aliases: consequent encroachment (when applied to a gap)
concept.definition: In SMC/ICT vocabulary, the 50% midpoint of a dealing range (a significant swing low to swing high), separating the premium half above from the discount half below. It serves as the reference for the methodology's value heuristic; outside SMC, a 50% midpoint is simply the midpoint of a range (also a Dow Theory retracement convention).
concept.intuition: The range's center of gravity: above it price is relatively expensive, below it relatively cheap, within that range.
concept.mechanics: Computed as (swing high + swing low)/2 of the chosen dealing range and drawn as a horizontal reference. SMC models use it to filter setups (longs below, shorts above) and as a mean-threshold reference on individual candles and gaps.
concept.failure_modes: The level moves whenever the analyst re-anchors the range, so it is unstable as a signal; price shows no documented obligation to react at a range midpoint.
concept.misconceptions: That equilibrium is a supply-demand balance price the market returns to; it is an arithmetic midpoint of an arbitrarily chosen range, not an economic equilibrium.
concept.example: A dealing range from 1800 to 1900 puts equilibrium at 1850; price stalls near 1850 on its way from the discount half toward the range high.
